purpose: Declares which committed files are REGENERABLE (rebuilt by the codegen/pipeline on each run). These files legitimately show as modified when codegen state evolves; their changes must be committed deliberately, never silently reverted or auto-committed. The repo-cleanliness guard consumes this to distinguish 'expected regenerable' from 'accidental junk'.
maintainerNote: Do NOT capture full content — only identity (glob) + generator + drift policy. Idempotent-write (skip rewrite when semantically equal) is deferred: current drivers are genuine regeneration drift, not deterministic re-write noise, so skip-if-equal adds no value until the writer is refactored to a stable emission order.

notes.notNoise: 2016-08-27 measured: subjects.metadata.json churn is real content drift (totalMethods 1333->1542), NOT timestamp noise — idempotent-write does not apply until stable emission order.
notes.guardBehavior: repo-clean guard only flags untracked (`??`) root junk; tracked `.json` under tests/e2e/translation are already ignored because they live under a whitelisted root and are tracked. Registry is for dev/pipeline transparency + future gates.
